mainTopic: אין מזל לישראל: צדקה and יראת שמים can overcome fate. Then a new משנה on מוקצה, and the dispute over whether the הלכה follows רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון.
overview: This amud finishes the idea of אין מזל לישראל: the stars do not lock in a Jew's fate. First 'ה tells אברהם that He will move the planet צדק (Jupiter) from west to east, and a פסוק in ישעיהו is read as a hint to this. Then come three stories. A man predicted to die from a snakebite is saved because he spared a poor friend embarrassment, and שמואל teaches that צדקה saves from death itself. רבי עקיבא's daughter is saved on her wedding day because she gave her portion to a poor man, and רבי עקיבא teaches the same lesson. רב נחמן בר יצחק was predicted to be a thief, and his mother protected him with a head covering and תפילה; the one time it slipped off, his nature showed itself. Next a new משנה allows cutting food for animals on שבת, but רבי יהודה forbids an animal that died on שבת because it is מוקצה. The גמרא lists who rules like רבי יהודה (עולא, רב, לוי) and who rules like רבי שמעון (שמואל, זעירי, רבי יוחנן). It then challenges רבי יוחנן's view from his rule to follow a סתם משנה, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: God moves Jupiter from west to east for אברהם
steps.stepSummary: Finishing 'ה's answer to אברהם: if the stars stand in your way, I will move them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it because צדק (the planet Jupiter) stands in the west that you think you can't have children? I will turn it around and put it in the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting 'ה's reply to אברהם. אברהם had said his מזל shows he will not have a son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם's reading of the stars was correct as far as the stars go. 'ה's answer is that He controls the stars and can change them for His people. So the stars do not have the final word for ישראל.

phrases.english: Is it because Jupiter stands in the west?
phrases.notes: Here 'ה is quoting אברהם's own reasoning from the stars.

phrases.english: I will turn it back and set it in the east.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the אברהם story from the previous daf, where 'ה tells אברהם: leave your astrology.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ה can rearrange the stars for ישראל, so their fate is not fixed by astrology.

steps.title: A פסוק in ישעיהו hints that Jupiter was moved for אברהם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads a פסוק as a hint to 'ה moving צדק to the east for אברהם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what the פסוק means: 'Who raised up from the east? צדק calls him to his feet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to support the idea that 'ה moved צדק (Jupiter) to the east for אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word צדק in the פסוק is read as the planet Jupiter. 'From the east' points to its new spot. לרגלו ('for his feet') is read as 'for his sake.' So the פסוק describes Jupiter being put in the east on אברהם's behalf.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written
At his feet; read here as 'for his sake'

steps.confusionAlert: צדק here is not only 'righteousness.' The דרשה works because צדק is also the Hebrew name of the planet Jupiter.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"Who raised up from the east,
Tzedek (Jupiter) calls him to his feet."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That 'ה moved Jupiter to the east for אברהם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו מא:ב, reading צדק as Jupiter and לרגלו as 'for his sake'.

steps.title: שמואל and אבלט: a man predicted to die comes back alive
steps.stepSummary: A second proof for אין מזל לישראל. אבלט predicts a man will die of a snakebite. שמואל says a Jew can be saved, and the man returns safely.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can also learn from שמואל that there is no מזל for ישראל. שמואל and אבלט were sitting while some people walked to the lake. אבלט said: 'That man will go and not come back. A snake will bite him and he will die.' שמואל said: 'If he is a Jew, he will go and come back.' While they sat, the man went and came back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof that ישראל is not bound by the stars. It tells of an astrologer's prediction that did not come true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבלט is a skilled astrologer, and his reading is not presented as foolish. שמואל's point is that a Jew's fate can be changed, so the star-based prediction may not hold. The man returning alive is the first half of the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no (binding) constellation for the Jewish people

phrases.english: And from Shmuel too we learn there is no constellation for Israel.
For Shmuel and Avlet were sitting,
and some people were going to the lake.
Avlet said to Shmuel:
This man will go and not come back;
a snake will bite him and he will die.
Shmuel said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי בַּר יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא, אָזֵיל וְאָתֵי.
phrases.english: If he is a Jew, he will go and come back.
While they were sitting, he went and came back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof (נמי, 'also') after the proof from אברהם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story of שמואל, where an astrologer's death prediction failed for a Jew.

steps.title: The snake is found dead in his bundle, and שמואל asks what he did
steps.stepSummary: אבלט finds a snake cut in two inside the man's load. This proves the danger was real, and שמואל asks what merit saved him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבלט got up and threw down the man's bundle. Inside he found a snake cut into two pieces. שמואל asked the man: 'What did you do?'
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows that the prediction was accurate: a deadly snake really was there. Then שמואל asks what merit saved the man, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Finding the snake shows אבלט's astrology was not wrong. The decree was real, but something overrode it. שמואל's question looks for the cause.

phrases.english: Avlet got up and threw down his bundle,
and found in it a snake
cut and lying in two pieces.
Shmuel said to him: What did you do?
phrases.notes: He is asking what merit saved the man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the danger from step 3 was real, then asks why the man survived.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which deed earned the man a rescue from his destined death.

steps.title: He secretly spared a poor man embarrassment
steps.stepSummary: The man explains that he protected a friend with no bread from embarrassment. שמואל calls it a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'Every day we put our bread together and eat. Today one of us had no bread and was embarrassed. I told them: I will collect the bread. When I reached him, I acted as if I took bread from him, so he would not be embarrassed.' שמואל said: 'You did a מצוה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The man answers שמואל's question by describing a quiet act of kindness. שמואל confirms it was a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deed was small but sensitive: he protected someone's dignity without anyone noticing. This act of צדקה is presented as what canceled the decree of death.

keyTerms.meaning: We put bread together (into a shared pool)

phrases.english: He said to him:
Every day we would put in bread
together and eat.
Today there was one of us
who had no bread,
and he was embarrassed.
I said to them:
I will get up and collect.
When I reached him,
I made myself look like one who took from him,
so that he would not be embarrassed.
He (Shmuel) said to him: You did a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's question from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He quietly saved a poor friend from embarrassment at the shared meal, which is a מצוה of צדקה.

steps.title: Charity saves from death itself
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that וצדקה תציל ממות means צדקה saves even from death itself, not only from a strange death.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל went out and taught: 'And צדקה saves from death' (משלי י:ב). This does not mean only from an unusual death. It means from death itself.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל draws a public lesson from the story. צדקה can cancel a death that was already decreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might read the פסוק narrowly: צדקה only turns a strange, terrible death into a normal one. שמואל's story shows it can remove the death entirely. This finishes the proof that a Jew's מזל can be overridden.
steps.whatToRemember: The stars may truly predict a Jew's fate, but מצוות, especially צדקה, can override that fate completely.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story is a classic source for the power of צדקה to change a heavenly decree, and for how important it is to protect another person's dignity.

phrases.english: Shmuel went out and expounded:
"And charity saves from death"
and not only from an unusual death,
but from death itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story of steps 3 to 5 into a lesson about a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: צדקה saves even from death itself, so a Jew's מזל is not final.

steps.title: Astrologers predict רבי עקיבא's daughter will die on her wedding day
steps.stepSummary: A third proof begins. Chaldean astrologers predict that רבי עקיבא's daughter will be killed by a snake on her wedding day.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can also learn from רבי עקיבא that there is no מזל for ישראל. רבי עקיבא had a daughter. Chaldean astrologers told him: 'On the day she enters the wedding canopy, a snake will bite her and she will die.' He was very worried about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a third story to prove אין מזל לישראל. This step sets up the frightening prediction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like אבלט, the כלדאי are treated as skilled astrologers whose prediction is a real threat. The story will show how the decree was avoided.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִדְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נָמֵי אֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: And from Rabbi Akiva too we learn there is no constellation for Israel.
For Rabbi Akiva had a daughter,
and Chaldean astrologers told him:
On the day she enters the wedding canopy,
a snake will bite her and she will die.
He was very worried about the matter.
phrases.notes: The word is masculine, so it's רבי עקיבא who was worried.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נָמֵי אֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third proof after the stories of אברהם and שמואל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי עקיבא's daughter and the astrologers' prediction.

steps.title: Her hairpin accidentally kills the snake
steps.stepSummary: On her wedding day the daughter sticks her hairpin into the wall. It happens to stab the snake's eye, and in the morning the dead snake comes out with the pin.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that day she took her hairpin and stuck it into the wall. It happened to go right into the snake's eye. In the morning, when she pulled the pin out, the snake came dragging out after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows that the predicted snake was really there, but it was killed before it could harm her. The explanation of why she was saved comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As in שמואל's story, the danger was real, which shows the astrologers were right about the stars. But the decree was overturned by what looks like coincidence. The גמרא will next ask what merit caused this.

phrases.english: On that day she took the hairpin
and stuck it into the wall;
it happened to sink into the eye of the snake.
In the morning, when she took it out,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא סָרֵיךְ וְאָתֵי חִיוְיָא בָּתְרַהּ.
phrases.english: the snake came dragging after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the prediction from step 7 was real but did not happen. The story continues next.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The predicted death was avoided, even though the snake really came.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks his daughter what she did
steps.stepSummary: After the snake is found dead, רבי עקיבא asks his daughter what good deed saved her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her father said to her: What did you do?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא asks his daughter which good deed earned her this rescue. The question sets up her answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The astrologers said she would die, yet she survived. רבי עקיבא assumes a מצוה must have protected her, so he asks which one. This matches שמואל's question in the earlier story.

phrases.english: Her father said to her:
What did you do?
phrases.notes: Meaning: what merit saved you from the snake?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the discovery of the dead snake by asking what merit caused the rescue.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which good deed saved the daughter from the predicted death.

steps.title: She gave her portion to a poor man
steps.stepSummary: The daughter explains that a poor man knocked during the wedding feast and nobody heard him, so she gave him her own portion. רבי עקיבא calls it a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: In the evening a poor man came and called at the door. Everyone was busy with the feast, and nobody heard him. I got up, took the portion you had given me, and gave it to him. He said to her: You did a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The daughter answers her father's question. She noticed a poor man that everyone else ignored and gave him her own food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She gave from her own share, on her own wedding night, when everyone else was too busy to notice. רבי עקיבא confirms that this act of צדקה is the מצוה that saved her.

phrases.english: She said to him:
In the evening a poor man came,
he called out at the door,
and everyone was busy with the feast,
and there was nobody who heard him.
I stood up and took my portion
that you had given me, and I gave it to him.
He said to her: You did a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She gave her own food to a poor man whom everyone else ignored. This act of צדקה protected her.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא teaches that charity saves from death itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא publicly teaches that the פסוק וצדקה תציל ממות means צדקה saves from death itself, not only from an unusual death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא went out and taught: 'And charity saves from death.' This does not mean only from an unusual death. It means even from death itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא draws a public lesson from his daughter's rescue. He reads the פסוק in its strongest sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might read the פסוק narrowly: צדקה only turns a strange, violent death into a normal one. רבי עקיבא proves from the story that it can cancel a decreed death entirely. This is the same lesson שמואל taught in Step 6, now confirmed by a second story.

keyTerms.meaning: and charity saves from death (משלי י:ב)

steps.whatToRemember: Two stories, one lesson: צדקה can cancel a decree of death completely. It does not only soften the way a person dies.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva went out and taught:
"And charity saves from death" —
not only from an unusual death,
but even from death itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the daughter's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: צדקה can cancel a decree of death entirely, which shows that a person's מזל can be changed.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק was predicted to be a thief
steps.stepSummary: A fourth proof that אין מזל לישראל begins. Astrologers tell רב נחמן בר יצחק's mother that her son will be a thief. She makes him always cover his head and tells him to pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: From רב נחמן בר יצחק too we learn that there is no מזל for Israel. Astrologers told his mother: Your son will be a thief. She did not let him uncover his head. She told him: Cover your head, so that the fear of Heaven will be upon you, and pray for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new proof story. This step sets up the prediction and the mother's response, and the next step shows the result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prediction is a bad נטייה (inclination) that comes with his birth sign. His mother does not accept it as fate. She fights it with יראת שמים and תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: the stars do not decide the fate of the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: אֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל does not mean the prediction was false. The prediction was accurate about his nature. The point is that a Jew's מזל is not locked in, and it can be overcome.

phrases.english: And from Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak as well we learn:
there is no constellation (fixed fate) for Israel.
For to the mother of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak
the Chaldean astrologers said:
Your son will be a thief.
She did not let him uncover his head.
She said to him: Cover your head,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתִיהְוֵי עֲלָךְ אֵימְתָא דִשְׁמַיָּא,
phrases.english: so that the fear of Heaven will be upon you,
and pray for mercy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק נָמֵי אֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another proof story to the series supporting אין מזל לישראל.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that אין מזל לישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב נחמן בר יצחק's predicted thievery and his mother's response.

steps.title: His head is uncovered and he takes dates
steps.stepSummary: While learning under a palm tree, his head covering falls off. He looks up, is overcome by desire, climbs the tree, and bites off a cluster of dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not know why she told him this. One day he was sitting and learning under a palm tree. The cloak fell off his head. He raised his eyes, saw the palm tree, and his desire overpowered him. He climbed up and bit off a cluster of dates with his teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by showing what happened the one time his head was uncovered. This completes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slip shows the thieving nature was real and was waiting inside him. As long as he kept his head covered with יראת שמים, it never came out. So his מזל was real, but it could be held back through effort and תפילה.
steps.whatToRemember: These stories show that a Jew's מזל can be changed or held back through צדקה, תפילה, and יראת שמים.

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה יָדַע אַמַּאי קָאָמְרָה לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He did not know why she was telling him this.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד יָתֵיב קָא גָרֵיס תּוּתֵי דִיקְלָא,
phrases.english: One day he was sitting and learning under a palm tree,
the cloak fell off of his head,
he raised his eyes and saw the palm tree,
his desire overpowered him,
he climbed up and bit off a cluster of dates with his teeth.
phrases.notes: The tree belonged to someone else.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא הֲוָה יָדַע אַמַּאי קָאָמְרָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story begun in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: אין מזל לישראל: a bad מזל can be held back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The one time his head was uncovered, the predicted nature appeared. This shows his mother's method had been working all along.

steps.title: New משנה: cutting food for animals on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that on שבת one may cut pumpkins for an animal and cut a carcass for dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We may cut pumpkins in front of an animal, and a carcass in front of dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new משנה with a new topic: preparing animal food on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows cutting the food so the animals can eat it. He makes no distinction about when the animal died. This suggests he is not concerned about מוקצה here.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may cut the pumpkins before an animal,
phrases.notes: The pumpkins had already been picked before שבת.

phrases.english: and the carcass before the dogs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic. The aggadic section has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting pumpkins for animals and a carcass for dogs is allowed on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids an animal that died on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the animal was not already dead before שבת, it is forbidden because it is not מוכן (prepared).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If it was not already a carcass before שבת, it is forbidden, because it is not prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the תנא קמא in one case: an animal that died on שבת itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that was alive when שבת began was not thought of as dog food at that time. It is therefore מוקצה, meaning set aside and not prepared for use. According to רבי יהודה, it may not be cut or even moved.

keyTerms.meaning: from what is prepared (for use on שבת)
set aside, not available for use on שבת

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה נְבֵלָה מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: if it was not already a carcass before שבת,
it is forbidden —
because it is not from what is prepared.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה נְבֵלָה מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the תנא קמא's ruling in the case of an animal that died on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that died on שבת is מוקצה and forbidden.

steps.title: עולא rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a memory sign. Then עולא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who holds there is מוקצה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was stated (sign: ער"ל שח"ז). עולא said: The הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a disagreement among אמוראים about which תנא to follow. This step gives the first view, עולא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters ער"ל שח"ז are a memory aid for the names of the אמוראים quoted in this series. עולא accepts רבי יהודה's view, so an animal that died on שבת is forbidden as מוקצה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
(Ayin, Reish, Lamed, Shin, Chet, Zayin — a mnemonic.)
phrases.notes: A memory aid for the names of the אמוראים in this series.

phrases.english: Ulla said: The הלכה is like Rabbi Yehuda

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: אָמַר עוּלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: מוקצה applies on שבת.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees and rules like רבי שמעון, who holds there is no מוקצה of this kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The הלכה is like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposing view to עולא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון is known from elsewhere to reject this type of מוקצה. According to שמואל, an animal that died on שבת may be cut for dogs, which is closer to the תנא קמא of our משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not named in our משנה. שמואל is referring to his well-known view from other sources, where he rejects this type of מוקצה.

phrases.english: (And Shmuel said: The הלכה is like Rabbi Shimon).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposes עולא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: this type of מוקצה does not apply.

steps.title: רב also rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds רב to the list of those who rule like רבי יהודה, alongside עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב also holds that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that רב agrees with עולא and rules like רבי יהודה that מוקצה applies on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא already ruled like רבי יהודה. Now the גמרא adds a second supporter, רב. The proof for this claim comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And also (adds another supporter to the same view)
The practical law follows the opinion of

phrases.english: And Rav also holds
the halakha is like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a supporter to עולא's side of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב rules like רבי יהודה: מוקצה applies on שבת.

steps.title: Proof for רב: the mats on ships
steps.stepSummary: We know רב's view from a case where רב forbade moving certain mats and שמואל permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know? From the mats on ships: רב forbade moving them, and שמואל permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רב holds like רבי יהודה. In the case of the ship mats, רב forbade moving them because of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding something that was not set aside for use before שבת is רבי יהודה's approach. שמואל permitted it, which fits his view like רבי שמעון. So the same dispute shows up here in a practical case.

keyTerms.meaning: Mats on ships (as the translation explains it)

phrases.english: From the case of the mats on ships,
where Rav prohibited and Shmuel permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim about רב.
steps.raayaObject: That רב rules like רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling forbidding moving the ship mats, against שמואל who permitted it.

steps.title: לוי also rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds לוי as another supporter of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי also holds that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names a third authority, לוי, who rules like רבי יהודה. The proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side of רבי יהודה now includes עולא, רב, and לוי. Like before, the גמרא states the claim first and then backs it up.

phrases.english: And Levi also holds
the halakha is like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third supporter to רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: Proof for לוי: checking a possible טריפה by the garbage heap
steps.stepSummary: On יום טוב, לוי would only examine a possibly טריפה animal while sitting by a garbage heap. If it turned out non-kosher, it would not even be usable for dogs, and he could not move it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in the case of לוי: when they brought him a possible טריפה on יום טוב, he would only examine it while sitting by a garbage heap. He said: maybe it will not turn out kosher, and then it is not even fit for dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves לוי's view from his practice. He examined questionable animals on יום טוב only next to a garbage heap, so that if the animal was not kosher, he could drop it right there without carrying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יום טוב, this animal was meant for people, not for dogs. If it turns out to be a טריפה, it was never 'prepared' for dogs, so it becomes מוקצה and may not be moved. That is exactly רבי יהודה's logic of מוכן.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that may be a טריפה (non-kosher because of a fatal defect)

steps.confusionAlert: לוי was not worried about eating forbidden meat. His concern was that if the animal turned out to be a טריפה, it would not have been 'prepared' even for dogs before יום טוב. It would then be מוקצה and could not be moved, so he examined it where it could be left lying.

phrases.english: As in this case of Levi:
when they would bring a possible tereifa before him
on a Festival,
he would not examine it
except when sitting by a garbage heap.
For he said: Perhaps it will not be found kosher,
and it would not be fit even for dogs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the evidence for the claim about לוי.
steps.raayaObject: That לוי rules like רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: לוי's practice of examining questionable animals on יום טוב only near a garbage heap.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון, and זעירי agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the other side. שמואל rules like רבי שמעון, and זעירי holds the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. And זעירי also holds that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats שמואל's ruling so it can list who agrees with him. It adds זעירי as a supporter, and the proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of רבי יהודה's supporters is done. Now the גמרא builds the list for רבי שמעון, who holds there is no מוקצה of this kind. שמואל's line is restated here as the heading of this new list.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
the halakha is like Rabbi Shimon;
and Ze'eiri also holds
the halakha is like Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Switches from רבי יהודה's supporters to רבי שמעון's supporters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל and זעירי rule like רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Proof for זעירי: he limits the משנה to a sacred animal
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says an animal that died may not be moved. זעירי explains this applies only to a consecrated animal, so an ordinary animal may be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: an animal that died may not be moved from its place. זעירי explained: this is about a consecrated animal. But an ordinary animal is fine to move.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves זעירי's view from how he read a משנה. He limited the ban on moving a dead animal to קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A consecrated animal may not be fed to dogs, so it has no use and is מוקצה no matter what. By limiting the משנה to קדשים, זעירי shows that an ordinary animal that died on שבת is usable for dogs and not מוקצה. That is רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Explained it / applied it to a specific case

phrases.english: As we learned: An animal that died —
one may not move it from its place;
and Ze'eiri explained it:
it refers to a consecrated animal.
But with a non-sacred animal — it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the evidence for זעירי's view.
steps.raayaObject: That זעירי rules like רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זעירי's reading that limits the משנה's ban to a consecrated animal.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds רבי יוחנן to רבי שמעון's side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן also said: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי יוחנן as another authority who rules like רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן is a major authority, so his support carries a lot of weight. This claim is about to be challenged in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan also said
the halakha is like Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third supporter to רבי שמעון's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Challenge: does רבי יוחנן really say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's ruling. רבי יוחנן also said the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, and an unattributed משנה is about to be quoted that seems to disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say that? But רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה. And we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי יוחנן rules like רבי שמעון. This step sets up the challenge, and the actual משנה is quoted at the start of the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a general rule: when a משנה is stated with no name attached, it is the הלכה. If an unattributed משנה follows רבי יהודה's view of מוקצה, then רבי יוחנן's two statements would contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (opens a challenge)
An unattributed משנה, stated without a name

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But Rabbi Yochanan said:
the halakha follows an unattributed mishna,
and we learned:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim made in the previous step about רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן rules like רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's general rule to follow a סתם משנה would clash with ruling like רבי שמעון, if an unattributed משנה follows רבי יהודה. The משנה is quoted next.
